age.evidence: pups aged postnatal day (PND) 14-25 were used for the present study

sex.evidence: In total, data from 66 animals were included in the study (37 females and 29 males).

dosing.evidence: DMT (Cayman chemical; Ann Arbor, MI, USA) was dissolved in 96% ethanol to a final stock solution of 500 μM, 10 μM, or 90 mM. On the experiment day, the stock solution was diluted ×1000 in ACSF to a final concentration of 500 nM, 10 μM, or 90 μM... bath applying DMT (5 mL). DMT was applied with a duration of 250-300 s.

handling.evidence: Mice were transferred through handling tunnels to the transport box. (Tunnel transfer only; no habituation handling protocol described.)

group_housing.evidence: All pups were housed with the mother until PND 21, where females and males were weaned and separated with a maximum of five same-sex mice per cage.

day_night_flipped.evidence: illuminated under a 12-h light/dark cycle (Lights on from 07:00 AM).

enrichment_housing.evidence: Cages were enriched with hiding places.

judge_notes: All three candidates agreed that no behavioural assays are present. The study is entirely ex vivo: whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology and Fura-2 calcium imaging in VTA brain slices. Both of these are excluded under the rubric as slice physiology and imaging, so the assays array is empty.

DMT was never administered to live animals. It was bath-applied to brain slices at 500 nM, 10 μM and 90 μM. The dosing entry follows the 2/3 candidate majority, which retained it for context with route 'other', no mg/kg conversion, and ethanol stock diluted in ACSF as the vehicle.
Handling is set to not_reported, following the 2/3 majority. The paper only describes moving mice to the transport box with handling tunnels, and this is not a habituation handling protocol.
Age is classified as juvenile (PND 14-25), following the 2/3 majority over 'adolescent'.
The DOI 10.1111/jnc.70463 was used unanimously by all candidates and is consistent with the peer-review link in the paper.
